description: 60 samples for prosodic boundary evaluation. Boundary annotations use | to mark: where boundaries SHOULD be (missing_boundary), where they ARE placed wrongly (extra_boundary), or where they naturally occur (natural).

scoring.1: Boundary missing or misplaced, effect is severe. Cannot recover intended sentence structure.
scoring.2: Boundary missing or misplaced, noticeably hurts listening but you can still follow.
scoring.3: Boundaries align naturally with syntactic and semantic structure.

utterances.text: When the dog bites the man screams for help.
utterances.boundary_annotation: When the dog bites | the man screams for help.
utterances.description: Without boundary after 'bites', listener parses 'the dog bites the man' as one phrase — then 'screams' has no subject and the sentence falls apart.
utterances.tts_text: When the dog bites the man screams for help.

utterances.text: While the hunter shot the deer ran into the woods.
utterances.boundary_annotation: While the hunter shot | the deer ran into the woods.
utterances.description: Without boundary after 'shot', listener hears 'the hunter shot the deer' — then 'ran into the woods' has no subject and makes no sense.
utterances.tts_text: While the hunter shot the deer ran into the woods.

utterances.text: After the boy left the girl started crying.
utterances.boundary_annotation: After the boy left | the girl started crying.
utterances.description: Without boundary after 'left', listener hears 'the boy left the girl' — then 'started crying' dangles with no clear subject.
utterances.tts_text: After the boy left the girl started crying.

utterances.text: When she cleans the house smells like lemons.
utterances.boundary_annotation: When she cleans | the house smells like lemons.
utterances.description: Without boundary after 'cleans', listener hears 'she cleans the house' — then 'smells like lemons' is unparsable.
utterances.tts_text: When she cleans the house smells like lemons.

utterances.text: While the mother cooked the children played outside.
utterances.boundary_annotation: While the mother cooked | the children played outside.
utterances.description: Without boundary after 'cooked', listener hears 'the mother cooked the children' — horrifying misparse, structure completely breaks.
utterances.tts_text: While the mother cooked the children played outside.

utterances.text: As the fire burned the building collapsed to the ground.
utterances.boundary_annotation: As the fire burned | the building collapsed to the ground.
utterances.description: Without boundary after 'burned', listener hears 'the fire burned the building' — then 'collapsed' has no subject.
utterances.tts_text: As the fire burned the building collapsed to the ground.

utterances.text: Before the teacher spoke the students had already left.
utterances.boundary_annotation: Before the teacher spoke | the students had already left.
utterances.description: Without boundary after 'spoke', listener hears 'the teacher spoke the students' — nonsensical verb usage, structure collapses.
utterances.tts_text: Before the teacher spoke the students had already left.

utterances.text: Since the workers finished the project moved forward quickly.
utterances.boundary_annotation: Since the workers finished | the project moved forward quickly.
utterances.description: Without boundary after 'finished', listener hears 'the workers finished the project' — then 'moved forward' has no subject.
utterances.tts_text: Since the workers finished the project moved forward quickly.

utterances.text: The horse raced past the barn fell down.
utterances.boundary_annotation: The horse raced past the barn | fell down.
utterances.description: Classic garden path. Without boundary, listener expects 'raced' as main verb — then 'fell down' seems to come from nowhere.
utterances.tts_text: The horse raced past the barn fell down.

utterances.text: The woman who whistles tunes pianos for a living.
utterances.boundary_annotation: The woman who whistles | tunes pianos for a living.
utterances.description: Without boundary after 'whistles', listener hears 'who whistles tunes' — then 'pianos' makes no sense as a continuation.
utterances.tts_text: The woman who whistles tunes pianos for a living.

utterances.text: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.
utterances.boundary_annotation: The quick brown | fox jumps over the lazy dog.
utterances.description: Boundary splits noun phrase 'quick brown fox' — listener cannot group the adjectives with the noun, sentence structure breaks.
utterances.tts_text: The quick brown, fox jumps over the lazy dog.

utterances.text: He was looking forward to the vacation.
utterances.boundary_annotation: He was looking | forward to the vacation.
utterances.description: Boundary splits phrasal verb 'looking forward to' — listener hears 'he was looking' then 'forward to the vacation' as unrelated, structure collapses.
utterances.tts_text: He was looking, forward to the vacation.

utterances.text: She fell asleep during the boring movie.
utterances.boundary_annotation: She fell | asleep during the boring movie.
utterances.description: Boundary splits compound verb 'fell asleep' — listener hears 'she fell' as a complete thought, then 'asleep' seems like a restart.
utterances.tts_text: She fell, asleep during the boring movie.

utterances.text: They could not believe what just happened.
utterances.boundary_annotation: They could | not believe what just happened.
utterances.description: Boundary splits modal from negation — listener hears 'they could' then 'not believe' as disconnected, cannot recover intended meaning.
utterances.tts_text: They could, not believe what just happened.

utterances.text: The president of the United States addressed the nation.
utterances.boundary_annotation: The president of | the United States addressed the nation.
utterances.description: Boundary splits prepositional phrase — listener hears 'the president of' dangling, then a new clause starting with 'the United States'.
utterances.tts_text: The president of, the United States addressed the nation.

utterances.text: I want to quickly finish my homework tonight.
utterances.boundary_annotation: I want to | quickly finish my homework tonight.
utterances.description: Boundary splits infinitive 'to quickly finish' — listener hears 'I want to' as complete, then 'quickly finish' as a command.
utterances.tts_text: I want to, quickly finish my homework tonight.

utterances.text: She has been running for three straight hours.
utterances.boundary_annotation: She has been | running for three straight hours.
utterances.description: Boundary splits progressive aspect 'has been running' — listener hears 'she has been' then 'running' as disconnected fragments.
utterances.tts_text: She has been, running for three straight hours.

utterances.text: He picked up his bag and walked out the door.
utterances.boundary_annotation: He picked | up his bag and walked out the door.
utterances.description: Boundary splits phrasal verb 'picked up' — listener hears 'he picked' then 'up his bag' as unrelated, structure collapses.
utterances.tts_text: He picked, up his bag and walked out the door.

utterances.text: They were about to leave when it started raining.
utterances.boundary_annotation: They were | about to leave when it started raining.
utterances.description: Boundary splits 'were about to' — listener hears 'they were' as complete, then 'about to leave' as a disjointed restart.
utterances.tts_text: They were, about to leave when it started raining.

utterances.text: She wanted to give up her seat on the crowded bus.
utterances.boundary_annotation: She wanted to give | up her seat on the crowded bus.
utterances.description: Boundary splits phrasal verb 'give up' — listener hears 'she wanted to give' then 'up her seat' as unrelated, structure collapses.
utterances.tts_text: She wanted to give, up her seat on the crowded bus.

utterances.text: She cooked dinner and he washed the dishes.
utterances.boundary_annotation: She cooked dinner | and he washed the dishes.
utterances.description: Missing boundary before coordinating conjunction — sounds rushed and run-together, but both clauses are still comprehensible.
utterances.tts_text: She cooked dinnerand he washed the dishes.

utterances.text: The dog barked loudly but nobody came to check.
utterances.boundary_annotation: The dog barked loudly | but nobody came to check.
utterances.description: Missing adversative boundary — sounds choppy and hurried, but sentence meaning is still recoverable.
utterances.tts_text: The dog barked loudlybut nobody came to check.

utterances.text: He opened the door and stepped outside into the rain.
utterances.boundary_annotation: He opened the door | and stepped outside into the rain.
utterances.description: Missing coordinating boundary — two actions run together unnaturally, but listener can still follow the sequence.
utterances.tts_text: He opened the doorand stepped outside into the rain.

utterances.text: The rain stopped so we went for a walk.
utterances.boundary_annotation: The rain stopped | so we went for a walk.
utterances.description: Missing resultative boundary — cause and effect blur together, sounds rushed but meaning is clear.
utterances.tts_text: The rain stoppedso we went for a walk.

utterances.text: She smiled warmly and greeted all her guests.
utterances.boundary_annotation: She smiled warmly | and greeted all her guests.
utterances.description: Missing coordinating boundary — actions run together without pause, sounds unnatural but followable.
utterances.tts_text: She smiled warmlyand greeted all her guests.

utterances.text: The phone rang but she didn't answer it.
utterances.boundary_annotation: The phone rang | but she didn't answer it.
utterances.description: Missing adversative boundary — contrast between clauses is lost, sounds flat and rushed but still comprehensible.
utterances.tts_text: The phone rangbut she didn't answer it.

utterances.text: He finished his coffee then left for work early.
utterances.boundary_annotation: He finished his coffee | then left for work early.
utterances.description: Missing temporal boundary — sequence of events runs together, sounds hurried but listener can still track the actions.
utterances.tts_text: He finished his coffeethen left for work early.

utterances.text: The store was closed so they drove back home.
utterances.boundary_annotation: The store was closed | so they drove back home.
utterances.description: Missing resultative boundary — cause and result blur, sounds choppy but meaning preserved.
utterances.tts_text: The store was closedso they drove back home.

utterances.text: The music stopped and everyone looked around.
utterances.boundary_annotation: The music stopped | and everyone looked around.
utterances.description: Missing coordinating boundary — two actions blend together, sounds rushed but followable.
utterances.tts_text: The music stoppedand everyone looked around.

utterances.text: The alarm went off but he slept right through it.
utterances.boundary_annotation: The alarm went off | but he slept right through it.
utterances.description: Missing adversative boundary — contrast is dulled, sounds unnatural but sentence still comes through.
utterances.tts_text: The alarm went offbut he slept right through it.

utterances.text: She picked up the phone and called her mother.
utterances.boundary_annotation: She picked | up the phone and called her mother.
utterances.description: Boundary splits phrasal verb 'picked up' — sounds like hesitation or system glitch, awkward but you can still follow.
utterances.tts_text: She picked, up the phone and called her mother.

utterances.text: We should probably leave soon to catch the bus.
utterances.boundary_annotation: We should | probably leave soon to catch the bus.
utterances.description: Boundary after modal — sounds like unnatural hesitation, awkward pause but sentence remains comprehensible.
utterances.tts_text: We should, probably leave soon to catch the bus.

utterances.text: The book on the table fell to the floor.
utterances.boundary_annotation: The book | on the table fell to the floor.
utterances.description: Boundary separates subject from its modifier — slightly disorienting but listener can regroup and follow.
utterances.tts_text: The book, on the table fell to the floor.

utterances.text: He bought a new car last weekend.
utterances.boundary_annotation: He bought | a new car last weekend.
utterances.description: Boundary between verb and object — sounds like an awkward pause, but sentence meaning is clear.
utterances.tts_text: He bought, a new car last weekend.

utterances.text: The children played in the park all afternoon.
utterances.boundary_annotation: The children played | in the park all afternoon.
utterances.description: Slightly early boundary before PP — sounds a bit choppy but sentence structure is still recoverable.
utterances.tts_text: The children played, in the park all afternoon.

utterances.text: She finished her work and went home early.
utterances.boundary_annotation: She finished | her work and went home early.
utterances.description: Boundary splits verb from object — sounds like hesitation, awkward but meaning preserved.
utterances.tts_text: She finished, her work and went home early.

utterances.text: The old man walked slowly down the street.
utterances.boundary_annotation: The old | man walked slowly down the street.
utterances.description: Boundary splits adjective from noun — sounds like a false start, awkward but sentence is followable.
utterances.tts_text: The old, man walked slowly down the street.

utterances.text: They decided to leave the party early.
utterances.boundary_annotation: They decided | to leave the party early.
utterances.description: Boundary between verb and infinitive complement — sounds like hesitation, noticeable but comprehensible.
utterances.tts_text: They decided, to leave the party early.

utterances.text: The rain stopped just before noon.
utterances.boundary_annotation: The rain | stopped just before noon.
utterances.description: Boundary between subject and verb — sounds like a system glitch, unnatural but sentence still comes through.
utterances.tts_text: The rain, stopped just before noon.

utterances.text: He always drives way too fast on the highway.
utterances.boundary_annotation: He always | drives way too fast on the highway.
utterances.description: Boundary between adverb and verb — sounds like unnatural hesitation, awkward but followable.
utterances.tts_text: He always, drives way too fast on the highway.

utterances.text: Although it was raining, we decided to go for a walk.
utterances.boundary_annotation: Although it was raining, | we decided to go for a walk.
utterances.description: Natural boundary at concessive clause edge — phrasing aligns with syntactic structure.
utterances.tts_text: Although it was raining, we decided to go for a walk.

utterances.text: The meeting was long, but everyone stayed until the end.
utterances.boundary_annotation: The meeting was long, | but everyone stayed until the end.
utterances.description: Natural boundary before adversative conjunction — major constituents grouped correctly.
utterances.tts_text: The meeting was long, but everyone stayed until the end.

utterances.text: She finished her work, then went home to cook dinner.
utterances.boundary_annotation: She finished her work, | then went home to cook dinner.
utterances.description: Natural boundary at temporal clause edge — phrasing feels natural and aligned.
utterances.tts_text: She finished her work, then went home to cook dinner.

utterances.text: Because the traffic was heavy, we took a different route.
utterances.boundary_annotation: Because the traffic was heavy, | we took a different route.
utterances.description: Natural boundary after causal subordinate clause — structure is clear and natural.
utterances.tts_text: Because the traffic was heavy, we took a different route.

utterances.text: If you finish your homework early, we can watch a movie.
utterances.boundary_annotation: If you finish your homework early, | we can watch a movie.
utterances.description: Natural boundary in conditional structure — clause edge feels right.
utterances.tts_text: If you finish your homework early, we can watch a movie.

utterances.text: The restaurant was crowded, so we ordered takeout instead.
utterances.boundary_annotation: The restaurant was crowded, | so we ordered takeout instead.
utterances.description: Natural boundary before resultative conjunction — phrasing aligns with meaning.
utterances.tts_text: The restaurant was crowded, so we ordered takeout instead.

utterances.text: While the baby was sleeping, the parents cleaned the house.
utterances.boundary_annotation: While the baby was sleeping, | the parents cleaned the house.
utterances.description: Natural boundary after temporal subordinate clause — phrases group correctly.
utterances.tts_text: While the baby was sleeping, the parents cleaned the house.

utterances.text: The concert started late, yet the audience enjoyed every moment.
utterances.boundary_annotation: The concert started late, | yet the audience enjoyed every moment.
utterances.description: Natural boundary before adversative conjunction — phrasing feels natural.
utterances.tts_text: The concert started late, yet the audience enjoyed every moment.

utterances.text: Since you're already here, you might as well stay for dinner.
utterances.boundary_annotation: Since you're already here, | you might as well stay for dinner.
utterances.description: Natural boundary at causal clause edge — phrasing aligns with syntactic structure.
utterances.tts_text: Since you're already here, you might as well stay for dinner.

utterances.text: After the storm finally passed, the sky turned brilliant orange.
utterances.boundary_annotation: After the storm finally passed, | the sky turned brilliant orange.
utterances.description: Natural boundary after temporal subordinate clause — clause edge feels right.
utterances.tts_text: After the storm finally passed, the sky turned brilliant orange.

utterances.text: The cat sat quietly on the warm windowsill.
utterances.boundary_annotation: The cat sat quietly | on the warm windowsill.
utterances.description: Natural phrasing — simple sentence with natural flow, no forced boundaries needed.
utterances.tts_text: The cat sat quietly on the warm windowsill.

utterances.text: Children play in the park every afternoon.
utterances.boundary_annotation: Children play in the park | every afternoon.
utterances.description: Natural phrasing — simple declarative with natural phrase grouping.
utterances.tts_text: Children play in the park every afternoon.

utterances.text: Fresh coffee smells wonderful in the morning.
utterances.boundary_annotation: Fresh coffee smells wonderful | in the morning.
utterances.description: Natural phrasing — descriptive sentence with natural prosodic flow.
utterances.tts_text: Fresh coffee smells wonderful in the morning.

utterances.text: The sun rises early during the summer months.
utterances.boundary_annotation: The sun rises early | during the summer months.
utterances.description: Natural phrasing — factual statement with natural boundary before temporal PP.
utterances.tts_text: The sun rises early during the summer months.

utterances.text: She reads a chapter before going to sleep.
utterances.boundary_annotation: She reads a chapter | before going to sleep.
utterances.description: Natural phrasing — routine activity with natural boundary before temporal clause.
utterances.tts_text: She reads a chapter before going to sleep.

utterances.text: The express train arrives at platform three.
utterances.boundary_annotation: The express train arrives | at platform three.
utterances.description: Natural phrasing — informational sentence with natural flow.
utterances.tts_text: The express train arrives at platform three.

utterances.text: Birds sing sweetly in the early springtime.
utterances.boundary_annotation: Birds sing sweetly | in the early springtime.
utterances.description: Natural phrasing — poetic observation with natural prosodic boundary.
utterances.tts_text: Birds sing sweetly in the early springtime.

utterances.text: The public library closes at nine o'clock.
utterances.boundary_annotation: The public library closes | at nine o'clock.
utterances.description: Natural phrasing — factual information with natural boundary before time PP.
utterances.tts_text: The public library closes at nine o'clock.

utterances.text: He waters all the garden plants every morning.
utterances.boundary_annotation: He waters all the garden plants | every morning.
utterances.description: Natural phrasing — daily routine with natural boundary before temporal adverbial.
utterances.tts_text: He waters all the garden plants every morning.

utterances.text: Ocean waves crash steadily against the rocky shore.
utterances.boundary_annotation: Ocean waves crash steadily | against the rocky shore.
utterances.description: Natural phrasing — natural phenomenon with natural boundary before directional PP.
utterances.tts_text: Ocean waves crash steadily against the rocky shore.
